correctness.rationale: Marking a non-singleton s-block and deleting it yields the exact normalized covariance; the positive coefficient power \(G(z)^{r-1}\) is strictly log-concave by Toeplitz two-minor convolution closure, proving the required strict decrease of the singleton mean in total size; the deterministic excess identity forces positive and negative endpoints. The r=1 boundary and uniform-occupancy transfer are proved separately. A fresh run of the exact checker passed 499367 assertions including independent brute-force enumerations, without substituting finite checks for infinite proof.

A separately known noncrossing-partition covariance threshold is for a distinct measure, not the unrestricted uniform set-partition law.

originality.rationale: The strict all-size sign order of conditional singleton-versus-size frequency covariances is a different theorem from classical Stirling block counts, nonsingleton generating-function real-rootedness, asymptotic unconditioned occupancy covariances, and known unconditional richness-frequency sign switches. The new step is a monotone exact normalized conditional covariance together with a positive-weight excess identity that forces one sign change; it is neither an immediate old table entry nor an implication of the checked comparison statements. The evidence is not an exhaustive historical priority guarantee.
residual_risks: Historical occupancy factorial-moment literature may contain a stronger implicit conditional order not located by available statement searches.
Some publisher papers were examined at abstract level only, so absence of a result in their full text cannot be asserted.

The complete text of a closely related modern published covariance study was not accessible through the attempted public page; its available summary concerns unconditional richness–frequency correlation rather than this fixed-richness cross-frequency theorem.
The exact integer position of the unique sign transition varies with n and k and has not been simplified into a closed threshold expression.

value.rationale: For a natural finite occupancy/frequency-of-frequencies problem, the result provides the full conditional interaction sign classification over all block sizes, including a genuine zero and the two-block exception. It identifies a positive large-block/singleton dependence despite negative small-block dependence, a structured one-transition phenomenon not inferable from a single marginal or unconditional sign law. This is relevant to fixed-richness sampling design; it does not claim downstream inference or optimality beyond the proved law.
